documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
19 yo M establishing adult primary care. Aging out of his pediatric office; mother came with him to the first part of the visit, he did the rest on his own.

HbSS sickle cell disease, picked up on newborn screen. Sees the adult sickle cell clinic at the regional hospital (moved over from pediatric hematology last year). On hydroxyurea 1000 mg daily for several years, folic acid 1 mg daily and penicillin VK 250 mg BID, all written by hematology. Says he takes the hydroxyurea most days, sometimes forgets the evening penicillin.

Rough year: four admissions for pain crises in the last 12 months, and two of those turned into acute chest syndrome. Last discharge was early this month. Feels back to himself now. Has had ACS several times going back to grade school. Told he has no working spleen. Right hip AVN was found on an x-ray at an orthopedic clinic when he was about 16; it aches now and then with a lot of walking but is not bothering him today.

No surgeries. NKDA.
FH: both parents carry sickle trait; younger brother also has sickle cell disease.
SH: lives in Springfield with his mother and brother. Part-time at a library circulation desk, taking classes at the community college. Never smoked. Drinks rarely, on a special occasion, and mostly avoids it since getting dry sets off pain. No drugs.

ROS: no fever, cough, chest pain, dyspnea, headache, vision change, priapism, leg ulcers. Mild right hip ache as above.

Exam: thin young man, comfortable. Sclerae anicteric today. Neck supple, no nodes. Lungs clear. Heart regular, no murmur. Abdomen soft, no tenderness, spleen and liver not felt. Right hip: full motion, mild discomfort at end internal rotation. Skin without ulcers. Neuro grossly normal.

A/P
1. HbSS sickle cell disease with frequent crises this year. Hematology owns hydroxyurea and its counts; he has a visit there in June. Drew a baseline CBC, CMP and urine albumin here so we have our own numbers. Hydration and cold-avoidance talk, he knows it well.
2. Functional asplenia. Fever 38.3 or higher = ED same day, he knows this. Continue penicillin per hematology. Requested pediatric vaccine records; never had MenB as far as he knows, so first dose of Bexsero today, second in about a month.
3. Right hip AVN. Stable symptoms. Watch.
4. Hx ACS. No current symptoms.
5. Health maintenance: HIV and hep C screening sent today, lipids. PHQ-2 0.

Return: nurse visit late May for MenB #2; see me after the hematology visit.

documents.title: Your lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Darnell, your blood work from Monday is back. Your hemoglobin is about 8, which is in your usual sickle cell range, and your kidney numbers and urine protein look good. Bilirubin is a little high, which is expected with sickle cell. Cholesterol is fine. Your HIV and hepatitis C screens are both negative. Nothing to change. See you after your June hematology visit.

documents.title: Pediatric Records Summary
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Records from prior pediatric office received by fax, 14 pages, scanned to media. Immunization history abstracted to the vaccine record. Childhood series complete per their record, including Hib, PCV13, two doses of PPSV23, MenACWY with booster at 16, HPV series and Tdap at 11. No MenB on file. Last well visit there 2018. Problem list matches ours: sickle cell disease SS, asplenia, hip AVN, history of acute chest.

documents.title: Nurse Visit - Immunization
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Here for 2nd Bexsero. Afebrile, feels well. Given L deltoid, tolerated. Sore arm after first dose only. MenB series complete. Reminded him to bring the hematology letter or have it sent after his June appointment.

documents.title: Adult Sickle Cell Clinic Follow-up
documents.author: hematology
documents.body:
Adult Sickle Cell Program, regional hospital hematology
Date of visit: 06/10/2019

Dear colleague,

I saw Darnell in follow-up for HbSS disease. It has been a hard twelve months: he counts four admissions for painful crises over that time, the most recent roughly two months back. He is doing well today.

Current medicines: hydroxyurea 1000 mg daily, folic acid 1 mg daily, penicillin VK 250 mg twice daily. Allergies: none known.

Vitals: T 37.2 C (99 F), BP 128/76, P 88, RR 16.
Well appearing, not in distress. Spleen is not palpable.

Labs today: Hgb 8.2 g/dL, Hct 24.5%, WBC 12,000, platelets 350,000, retic 10%, HbF 5%.

Impression: HbSS disease at his usual hemoglobin with brisk reticulocytosis. Functional asplenia. Right femoral head AVN and prior acute chest syndrome by history.

Plan: continue hydroxyurea 1000 mg daily, folic acid and penicillin without change. Return to clinic in 3-4 months, labs at that visit.

Thank you for sharing his care.
Adult Sickle Cell Program

documents.title: Emergency Department Note
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
Regional hospital ED, seen 09/16/2019.

19M with HbSS, functional asplenia, R femoral head AVN. Came in with deep aching bone pain in both arms and legs, started after a cold rainy weekend at an outdoor event. Same kind of pain he has had since childhood, usually set off by cold or getting dehydrated. Hematology clinic visit about 3 months ago.
Meds: folic acid 1 mg daily, penicillin VK 250 mg BID, hydroxyurea 1000 mg daily. NKDA.
T 37.2 C, BP 128/76, HR 88, RR 18, SpO2 97% RA. Uncomfortable, mild distress. Lungs clear.
Hgb 8.2, Hct 24.5, retic 4.5%, LDH 350, indirect bili 2.1. Smear: sickled red cells.
Imp: vaso-occlusive pain crisis. IV fluids and IV analgesia per sickle cell pathway, admitted to medicine.

documents.author: hospital medicine
documents.body:

Dx: sickle cell vaso-occlusive crisis.
Course: IV hydration and IV pain control, pain improved over three days, no fever, no chest symptoms, no oxygen requirement. Home on usual medicines.

documents.title: Orthopedic Follow-up
documents.author: orthopedics
documents.body:
Outside orthopedic group, visit 06/15/2020

Re: Darnell Grant, 20 y/o M, HbSS, R femoral head osteonecrosis, seen again by us at the request of his PCP.

He describes six months of right groin pain, a dull ache that builds as he walks and eases when he rests. No injury, fevers or weight loss. He has been admitted twice in the last year with sickle cell pain crises.
Meds: folic acid 1 mg daily, penicillin VK 250 mg BID, hydroxyurea 1000 mg daily. NKDA.

Exam R hip: range of motion full; internal rotation reproduces his pain. No warmth, erythema or swelling about the joint.

Labs: Hgb 8.5, WBC 12,000, plt 450,000, ESR 20, CRP 2.0 mg/L.
Radiographs R hip: irregular contour of the femoral head with subchondral sclerosis. No fracture, no dislocation.

Impression: R femoral head AVN in sickle cell disease, symptomatic. Inflammatory markers do not suggest infection.
Plan: activity modification, limit impact and prolonged walking. Return as needed if symptoms progress.

Hip still aches on long walks; he has been taking the bus more. No crises since February. Hematology visits by phone this spring, he says counts were similar.
Meds unchanged: hydroxyurea 1000 daily, folic acid 1 mg, penicillin VK 250 BID. NKDA.
SH: still at the library part time, it reopened last month. Online classes. No tobacco, rare alcohol.
ROS negative otherwise.
Exam: well. Lungs clear. Heart regular, no murmur. Abdomen soft, no organomegaly. R hip with end-range internal rotation pain. Skin clear, no leg ulcers.
PHQ-2 1.
A/P: HbSS, at his baseline. Annual CBC, CMP and urine albumin today. Hip AVN per ortho. Flu shot in the fall. MenACWY booster due next year (5 years from his last at 16). Return in a year, or sooner for anything.

documents.title: Office Visit - Fatigue
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
CC: tired, short of breath.
S: Several weeks of steadily worse fatigue, now winded on one flight of stairs and walking from the bus. No pain crisis in the last 6 months. No fever, cough, chest pain, sick contacts. No bleeding, black stools or blood in urine. Eating the same as always. Taking hydroxyurea and penicillin. Asked about folic acid: "I think I ran out a while ago." Fill history from the pharmacy shows last folic acid fill in March.
O: Pale. Scleral icterus. Lungs clear, no crackles. Heart regular. Abdomen soft; spleen tip felt about 2 cm below the left costal margin, nontender. No edema.
A/P
1. Fatigue and exertional dyspnea, HbSS. More anemic-looking than his baseline, jaundiced. Concern for folate depletion off supplement on top of his hemolysis. CBC, retic, folate, LDH, bili, haptoglobin now.
2. Palpable spleen, new on our exams. Add splenomegaly to the list, recheck on follow-up.
3. Folic acid lapsed since spring; off the active list until labs are back, then I will send a new script.
Return precautions given: fever, chest pain, worsening SOB, pain crisis = ED.

documents.title: Same-day CBC
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hgb 7.8 (his usual is low 8s), MCV 102, retic only 1%, LDH 420, total bili 3.1 / direct 0.5. Retic is far lower than his usual 4-10%: marrow not keeping up. Waiting on folate and haptoglobin.

Messaged the sickle cell clinic with the results.

To Disability Services:

Darnell Grant is a patient of this practice with sickle cell disease, a lifelong condition. Episodes of severe pain can occur without warning and may require emergency care or hospitalization. Staying hydrated and warm lowers that risk.

Please allow him to keep water with him in class and to take restroom breaks as needed, to dress for warmth in cold rooms, and to make up work or exams missed for medical care.

Please contact our office with questions.

Primary Care Physician

documents.title: Emergency Department Note
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
Regional hospital ED, 06/13/2025, evening.
25 y/o M, HbSS, functional asplenia. Abrupt severe LUQ pain this evening going up into the L shoulder. For about a week before: sore throat, fevers, worn out, better with rest and fluids over the last couple of days. No fall, no blow to the abdomen, no sports.
Meds: hydroxyurea 1000 mg daily, folic acid 1 mg daily, PCN VK 250 mg BID. NKDA.
BP 90/60, HR 120, RR 22, T 37.8.
Pale, sweaty. Abd: LUQ tender with guarding; bowel sounds present and normal; no rebound, not rigid.
Hgb 9.8, WBC 15,000, plt 250,000. AST 45, ALT 50. Monospot positive.
Bedside/formal US: enlarged spleen, hypoechoic area c/w subcapsular hematoma.
Imp: atraumatic splenic laceration with subcapsular hematoma in the setting of recent infectious mononucleosis. Fluid resuscitation started, surgery consulted, admitted.

documents.title: Discharge Summary
documents.author: general surgery
documents.body:
Admit 06/13/2025 - Discharge 06/17/2025. Surgical service.
Dx: splenic laceration, subcapsular hematoma, nonoperative management. Recent mononucleosis.
Course: IV fluids, bed rest, serial hemoglobins, which held steady. Heart rate and blood pressure normalized within the first day. No transfusion. No operation. Hydroxyurea and home meds continued. Pain controlled and tolerating diet at discharge.
Instructions: no lifting over 10 lb, no contact sports or strenuous activity until seen in surgery clinic. Return for worse abdominal pain, dizziness or fainting.
Follow-up: PCP 1 week; surgery clinic 6-8 weeks.

documents.title: Hospital Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
TCM visit. Records from the regional hospital reviewed (ED note and discharge summary arrived 6/19; spoke with pt by phone 6/18 to set this up).
Admitted 6/13-6/17 with an atraumatic splenic laceration and subcapsular hematoma after a week of what turned out to be mono (monospot +). Managed without surgery, no transfusion.
Today: LUQ soreness down to a 2, only with twisting. Sore throat gone, no fever since discharge. Eating fine. Staying off work this week, library is holding his hours.
Meds unchanged, reconciled: hydroxyurea 1000 mg daily, folic acid 1 mg daily, penicillin VK 250 mg BID.
Exam: tired-looking but comfortable. Abdomen soft, mild LUQ tenderness, no guarding; spleen not examined deeply.
A/P

documents.title: Emergency Department Note
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
Regional hospital ED, 12/12/2025.
25 y/o M with HbSS and functional asplenia; splenic laceration about six months ago, managed without surgery. Two days of increasing fatigue, yellow eyes and dark urine. Was admitted here 11/29-12/3 for a pain crisis and got a red cell transfusion on 12/2, ten days ago.
Meds: folic acid 1 mg daily, penicillin VK 250 mg BID, hydroxyurea 1000 mg daily. NKDA.
T 37.8, BP 130/80, HR 105, RR 18.
Scleral icterus. Mild splenomegaly. No rash. No lymphadenopathy.
Hgb 7.0 (baseline about 9). T bili 3.5, direct 0.8. LDH 600. Haptoglobin <10. Retic 15%. DAT positive; negative before the transfusion.
Imp: delayed hemolytic transfusion reaction. Blood bank notified, hematology consulted. Admitted for monitoring; avoid further transfusion if at all possible.

documents.title: Discharge Summary
documents.author: hospital medicine
documents.body:
Admit 12/12/2025 - Discharge 12/14/2025.
Dx: delayed hemolytic transfusion reaction after 12/2 transfusion. HbSS.
Course: observed with daily labs; hemoglobin held without further transfusion. Blood bank antibody workup sent, results to his hematologist. Hematology saw him in house. Folic acid and hydroxyurea continued. No pain crisis during the stay.
Important: any future transfusion only after his hematologist and the blood bank are contacted.
Follow-up: PCP within 1 week; hematology clinic early January.

conditions.label: Sickle cell disease with vaso-occlusive crisis

documents.title: Hospital Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
TCM. ED note and discharge summary received yesterday and reviewed. We had no records from the 11/29-12/3 crisis admission; pt filled in the history: pain crisis in the cold, admitted, one unit of blood on 12/2. Then on 12/10 he started getting tired and yellow, and urine went dark, back to the ED 12/12. Delayed hemolytic transfusion reaction, DAT positive, no more blood given, home 12/14.
Today: still tired but better each day. Eyes less yellow, urine lighter. Pain from the crisis gone. No fever, chest pain, SOB.
Meds reconciled, unchanged: hydroxyurea 1000 mg daily, folic acid 1 mg daily, penicillin VK 250 mg BID.
Exam: tired but comfortable. Mild scleral icterus. Lungs clear. Heart regular. Abdomen soft, spleen tip palpable, nontender.
A/P
1. DHTR, improving clinically. CBC and bili today. Recheck in 3-4 weeks. Added a transfusion alert to his chart: contact hematology and blood bank before any transfusion.
2. VOC late Nov, resolved.
3. HbSS: hematology early January.
ED for fever, worsening jaundice, chest pain or breathlessness.
